definition: AI-assisted virtualization software is a type of technology that combines the principles of virtualization with advanced artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms.
details: This software is designed to improve efficiency and management of virtual environments and resources. This technology has been used in cloud computing and for various industries.

explainer.lead: AI-assisted virtualization software uses AI to help decide how shared computing resources should be managed and divided. It aims to keep virtual environments running efficiently by predicting needs, automating routine work, and reducing wasted resources.

tiers.eli5: Imagine several people sharing one kitchen, with a helper watching when they usually cook and what they need. The helper can get the right equipment ready and move things around so nobody waits unnecessarily or leaves useful space idle. AI-assisted virtualization does something similar for the shared resources inside computers.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it in cloud computing, data centers, and network function virtualization, using real-time and historical operational data to guide provisioning, maintenance, and resource allocation. Machine learning, deep learning, and neural networks can support predictions about demand or future problems. Implementation can be technically difficult and costly, while algorithmic bias, security vulnerabilities, governance, ethics, and regulation remain important concerns.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, at time t, the system uses real-time and historical operating data D_t to predict resource requirements or potential issues, then chooses management actions and resource assignments A_t based on demand and need. Its objectives include proactive management, improved performance, and reduced resource wastage. Known limits include implementation complexity and cost, along with risks involving algorithmic bias, security, governance, ethics, and regulation.

explainer.example: In a data center, the software might analyze past and current resource use, predict that demand will rise, and provision additional resources before performance suffers. When demand falls, it can reassign those resources rather than leaving them unused.

usedIn.name: Cloud computing
usedIn.detail: Optimizing resource use and reducing costs.

explainer.intuition: Virtualization divides computing resources among different uses; adding AI gives the system a way to learn from operations and adjust that division as needs change. Instead of relying only on fixed rules or manual intervention, it can anticipate requirements and act on them.
howItWorks: Gather real-time and historical data about the virtual environment.
Use AI techniques to identify patterns and predict future problems or resource needs.
Turn those predictions into management decisions, such as automating provisioning or routine maintenance.
Assign resources dynamically according to demand and need, then continue learning from ongoing operations.
explainer.whyItMatters: Better predictions and automated adjustments can improve performance, reduce wasted resources, and lower cloud costs. They can also support proactive maintenance, helping managers address potential problems before they disrupt a virtual environment.
misconceptions: It is not simply conventional virtualization: the AI component adds prediction, decision-making, and adaptive management.
It does not make management risk-free or effortless: predictions can be affected by bias and security problems, and deployment can be complex and expensive.
